title: The Deadly Secrets
setting: A 30th birthday party in a small town

victim.name: Meredith Marsh
victim.description: The birthday girl—30, a waitress at the Sunrise Café—who dropped dead in her own hallway after a toast meant to celebrate her. The smile hadn't even left the guests' faces when her body betrayed her: fighting for air, fists locked, tongue thrusting past her lips. Whatever killed her acted fast, and cruelly.

cold_case_victim.name: Adam Green
cold_case_victim.description: Twenty years ago, a charismatic young tenant in Rose White's duplex—found hanging in his room with a note nearby. The town called it suicide; the family refused an autopsy on religious grounds. Adam had migraines, a bright future, and secrets the grave kept—until tonight.

intro_narrative: The porch lights of the Marsh house glow honey-yellow against a sky bruised with dusk. You shouldn't feel out of place here—you're Nick Vince, ex-detective, now criminology lecturer—but Tai Marsh insisted you come as a guest, not a badge. Meredith was your student once: sharp, curious, the kind who asked uncomfortable questions in the best way. Lately she hired you privately, voice low over coffee, to dig into her sister Emma's boyfriend, Alvin Mani. Nothing proven yet—just instincts she couldn't shake. Inside, the rooms smell of vanilla cake and someone's citrus cologne. Balloons drift in the archway. Tai is pouring drinks with a smile that doesn't reach his eyes. Alvin and Emma linger near the window, shoulders touching. Rose White has brought a casserole like a peace offering. Daniel Brown—'Film' to everyone—circulates with a recorder, always hunting audio for his podcast 'Crime in a Small Town.' Natalie Apple, who pulls pints at the Rusty Anchor, is trading jokes near the bar. Leon Rock lingers near the door with his wife Dr. Lili Rock, clearly not planning to stay long. Lili checks her phone between polite laughs. Elliot Holdman, guitarist for Skulls of Chaos, tunes an imaginary fretboard in the corner. Meredith appears with frosting on her thumb, laughing, alive. You raise a plastic cup of something sparkling and pretend you're only here for the cake. Somewhere beneath the music, your old instincts hum. In a town this size, every secret has an audience. Tonight feels like a ledger about to balance—in blood.
murder_event_narrative:
Tai taps a knife against his champagne flute until the room hushes. 'To Meredith,' he says, voice thick, '—my brilliant wife, and the best thing this town ever lucked into.' Glasses lift; someone whoops. The toast goes down warm and loud.

The music gets louder. Meredith dances with Emma, then with Tai, then lets Daniel spin her once for the joke of it. You almost believe the danger you sensed was only nerves.

Later, Emma's smile tightens. She guides Meredith toward the hallway, away from the speakers. You catch the edge of it—'Dad's will,' 'fair share,' 'don't shut me out'—before the bass swallows the words.

Then Meredith stumbles. Her hand claws at her throat; her breath comes in shredded gasps. Her fists lock so hard the knuckles bleach white. Her tongue pushes past her teeth, obscene and involuntary. Someone screams. The music dies mid-note.

Dr. Lili Rock is already there, fingers on Meredith's wrist, eyes on her pupils. Color drains from Lili's face. 'Call an ambulance,' she snaps, though her voice says she knows it's futile. She works anyway—until she stills, shoulders sagging.

'Meredith Marsh is dead,' Lili says to the stunned hush.

You step forward without thinking—the old reflex. Your voice cuts through shock: 'Nobody leaves this house.'

secret.text: Meredith was secretly three months pregnant—only her doctor knew from labs.

initial.prompt: Meredith Marsh wears a paper crown slightly askew and genuine joy like it's easier than breathing. Tonight the world is supposed to be cake and playlists—not anyone else's drama.

choices.text: Happy birthday, Meredith. How's thirty feel?
choices.response: Like I'm finally allowed to stop apologizing for my own life. Also—sore feet. Café shifts don't care about crowns.

clue.text: Meredith is upbeat about turning thirty—mentions long café shifts.

choices.text: Tai went all out for this.
choices.response: He always does when guilt nibbles. I love him for it. I also wish he'd sleep.

clue.text: Meredith senses Tai's stress/guilt beneath the party effort.

choices.text: You still want me looking into Alvin?
choices.response: You told me he's a recovering alcoholic — and I believe he's trying. Natalie says he's been clean for months. But Emma doesn't know any of this, and she's falling hard. If he relapses, or if there's more we don't know about his past… she deserves someone who'll stick. Just keep your eyes open. For her.

clue.text: Meredith knows about Alvin's alcoholism from Nick's investigation — consulted Natalie to confirm sobriety. Still worries about Emma not knowing the full picture.

choices.text: You and Emma okay?
choices.response: Sisters oscillate. She'll get mushy after cake—right now she's got her guard up. Family money does that.

clue.text: Meredith hints at tension with Emma around family money—expects resolution later.

initial.prompt: Natalie Apple moves like she owns every surface she touches—elbows on counters, easy grin. She winks at you with the familiarity of someone who knows how you take your coffee and your secrets.

choices.text: Working off the clock tonight?
choices.response: Every party needs a bartender, and I don't trust anyone else behind a counter. Tai hired me for the evening — said he wanted it done right.

clue.text: Tai hired Natalie to bartend the party—she takes the job seriously.

choices.text: How do you know Alvin?
choices.response: He's a regular. Used to order the hard stuff. Now when he comes in, I pour him soda, we talk. That's our thing now.

clue.text: Natalie confirms Alvin is a regular at the Anchor—used to drink hard, now sticks to soda. She watches out for him.

choices.text: Meredith ever hang at the pub?
choices.response: Shifts and sisters keep her busy—when she shows, she tips like sin and asks after everyone by name.

clue.text: Natalie knows Meredith socially from the pub—positive rapport.

choices.text: Behaving yourself tonight?
choices.response: Always. You're the one who can't stop glancing over. Relax—nobody's watching. Go mingle, detective. I'll save you the good glass.

clue.text: Natalie and Nick exchange a private moment—keeping their relationship under wraps at the party.

post_initial.prompt: Natalie stands behind the counter like it's the only thing holding her up. The easy confidence is gone—what's left is someone replaying the night in her head.

choices.text: Walk me through every pour before the toast.
choices.response: Wine for the crowd. For Alvin—water only, from the filtered tap into a clean cup. I told Tai which glass was Alvin's so he'd know when handing them out. Then before the toast I went over to Alvin and told him not to worry about his glass—I got him covered.

clue.text: Natalie poured water for Alvin and told Tai which glass was his. She then reassured Alvin personally before the toast.

choices.text: Meredith was pregnant and avoiding alcohol. Did she say anything to you about the drinks?
choices.response: She came up to me at the bar and asked which glass was Alvin's. I told her — the water. She just nodded and walked away. I didn't think anything of it at the time.

clue.text: Meredith asked Natalie which glass was Alvin's water — she knew exactly which cup to target for the swap.

choices.text: Meredith came to you about Alvin, didn't she?
choices.response: She did. She knew he was a regular at my bar, so she came in and asked me straight—is he still drinking? I told her the truth: he's been clean for months. She seemed relieved, but she said she still wasn't sure he was good enough for Emma.

clue.text: Meredith consulted Natalie about Alvin's drinking—Natalie confirmed his sobriety but Meredith still had doubts about him.

choices.text: What's Alvin's real story at the Anchor?
choices.response: It's not some overnight thing. He comes in, orders soda, fights the urge. Every single time. That takes guts.

clue.text: Natalie confirms Alvin's recovery arc—credibility as witness to his sobriety tonight.

choices.text: Leon seems wound tight tonight. You notice anything at the Anchor?
choices.response: Lawyers love whiskey and bad luck. Leon chases losses on poker night—I've cut him off more than once. Lili doesn't need that noise.

clue.text: Natalie attests to Leon's gambling and secret bar losses—Lili may not know the extent.

choices.text: Did Meredith ever see Leon at one of those poker nights?
choices.response: About a month ago. Meredith came in for a quiet drink and walked straight into Leon's worst session. He was down bad — I mean white-knuckle, loosening-the-tie bad. She saw the whole thing. Didn't say a word to him that night, just watched. Next day Leon came back alone, ordered a double, and asked me who else was in the room. He was rattled, Nick. The kind of rattled that doesn't go away.

clue.text: Natalie confirms Meredith witnessed Leon losing badly at a poker night about a month ago. The next day Leon came back asking who else saw.

choices.text: We need to talk about us. If this turns into a real investigation, someone's going to notice.
choices.response: Then let them notice. I'm more worried about you right now than what people think.

clue.text: Natalie and Nick's hidden relationship could surface in the investigation—she's choosing honesty with him over caution.

choices.text: Alvin seemed extra nervous tonight—even before all this. You know why?
choices.response: He was going to propose. Tonight, after the cake. Had the ring in his jacket pocket—showed it to me last week at the bar, hands shaking like a kid. He said, 'Natalie, if I can stay clean and do this one thing right, maybe I deserve her.' He never got the chance.

clue.text: Alvin planned to propose to Emma tonight—had a ring in his pocket. Natalie was the only one who knew.

natalie_meredith_water_detail.prompt: Natalie steadies a breath—details are her religion.

choices.text: Could anyone confuse Alvin's cup after you poured?
choices.response: I poured it, I know what went in. But after that? Tai took the tray out. People were moving around, bumping into things. I wasn't standing guard over every glass.

clue.text: Natalie affirms Alvin's cup began as water—later handling is the vulnerability point.

choices.text: How long are we going to keep pretending this is casual?
choices.response: You're sixty. I'm thirty-five. This town would have a field day. But yes—it's real. Has been for a while. It stays between us.

clue.text: Natalie confirms a secret romantic relationship with Nick Vince—hidden due to the age gap and small-town gossip.

secret.text: Tai stole proprietary code from Delta AI as a safety net—and Alvin discovered it.

initial.prompt: Tai Marsh moves between couch and kitchen like a man hosting a spreadsheet—every smile timed, every laugh one beat late. His eyes never quite settle.

choices.text: You look wired for a man throwing his wife a party.
choices.response: Delta AI doesn't sleep, and neither do I lately. Deadlines, demos—Meredith deserves one night that's actually about her.

clue.text: Tai cites brutal Delta AI workload—admits he's distracted despite the celebration.

choices.text: How are you and Meredith?
choices.response: Solid. We're trying—for things, I mean. The usual marriage stuff. She lights up a room; I'm just the guy who pays for the Wi-Fi.

clue.text: Tai describes the marriage as 'solid' but deflects with humor—little concrete detail.

choices.text: Alvin Mani and your sister-in-law seem pretty serious.
choices.response: He wasn't on the guest list — Emma brought him last minute. I wasn't expecting to see him tonight. He's got money, she's got drive — Meredith worries he's not the settling type, but that's sisters talking.

clue.text: Tai was surprised Alvin showed up — he wasn't formally invited. Emma brought him last minute.

choices.text: Why did you want me here tonight, really?
choices.response: Meredith likes you. And… I thought having a lecturer around might keep the conversation civil. Crime stories for Film, not real ones.

clue.text: Tai says Meredith wants Nick here—hopes his presence keeps talk 'civil.'

post_initial.prompt: After Meredith falls, Tai's hosting mask shatters. He's still standing, but like a man who's forgotten how knees work.

choices.text: Walk me through every second after the toast.
choices.response: We drank. Music on. I saw Meredith dancing—God, she looked happy. Then Emma pulled her away and I poured myself another drink.

clue.text: Tai confirms Meredith was fine immediately after the toast—collapse came later, after Emma spoke with her.

choices.text: Where were you when glasses were poured for the toast?
choices.response: Natalie handled the pours. She told me which glass was Alvin's so I could get it to him. I don't know why. I carried the tray out, called everyone in.

clue.text: Natalie told Tai which glass was Alvin's. Tai carried the tray out—he had direct access to every glass.

choices.text: Alvin's glass had water, not wine. Did you touch it?
choices.response: I moved trays—I might've nudged his glass adjusting the lineup. So did half a dozen hands.

clue.text: Tai gets defensive about touching Alvin's glass—admits possible contact during tray adjustments.

choices.text: How were things between Alvin and Meredith tonight?
choices.response: Tense. Meredith cornered him early on — I didn't hear what about, but Alvin's face went dark. He walked away and she just stood there watching him. I figured it was Emma stuff — big-sister interrogation.

clue.text: Tai saw Meredith confront Alvin at the party — Alvin didn't take it well. Possible conflict if Alvin knew she was investigating him.

choices.text: Alvin says you have a Monday meeting that could end your career.
choices.response: He… he told you? Nick, that's—look, people take snippets home from work all the time. Alvin's blowing a backup plan into treason.

clue.text: Under pressure, Tai minimizes stolen Delta code as a 'backup plan'—panicked rather than denying outright.

choices.text: Emma and Meredith were arguing right before the collapse. What do you know?
choices.response: That wasn't the first time. The will fight has been going on for months — Emma showing up unannounced, Meredith locking herself in the bedroom after calls. Last week Emma slammed our front door so hard the picture frames fell off the wall. And Emma… you know what she can do with her hands.

clue.text: Tai reveals the sisters' conflict has been escalating for months — and pointedly reminds Nick of Emma's lethal martial arts skills.

choices.text: Rose gave you that little red bottle for the rats—what did you do with it?
choices.response: Rat droppings in the garage—she handed me the red dropper bottle. I brought it back to her at the party, minutes before the toast. Pressed it into her hands; she dropped it in her bag.

clue.text: Tai claims Rose gave him rodenticide in a red bottle for rats — and that he returned it to her at the party before the toast.

choices.text: Was Meredith seeing any doctors recently?
choices.response: She had a full checkup with Lili last week. Blood work, everything. She came back and said it was all fine — nothing to worry about. So you tell me, Nick — how does someone get a clean bill of health and die a week later? Either Lili missed something, or she's not telling us the whole truth.

clue.text: Tai says Meredith had a full checkup with Lili just last week — everything was supposedly fine. Either Lili missed something or she's holding back.

tai_poison_window.prompt: You press the timeline around the glasses.

choices.text: Natalie says she poured water for Alvin. You had the tray after that?
choices.response: Then I had the tray. I was the last hand on several cups before the pour. If you're asking could someone dose a drink—yes. Could. Doesn't mean did.

clue.text: Tai admits he was the last person with hands on multiple cups right before the toast—including proximity to Alvin's water.

tai_code_pressure.prompt: You lean in—Monday isn't abstract anymore.

choices.text: Who else knew you were cornered?
choices.response: Emma warned me but I asked her not to tell her sister. Meredith… she knew I was stressed. She didn't know the filing Alvin waved at me. I thought I had the weekend.

clue.text: Tai says Emma warned him but he swore her to secrecy from Meredith; he still believed he had the weekend before Alvin's report.

suspects.name: Emma Shield
suspects.role: Meredith's younger sister, martial arts champion, cheer coach

secret.text: Emma is drowning in personal debt—near bankruptcy—hidden behind trophy polish.

initial.prompt: Emma Shield fills a doorway without trying—shoulders squared by years of kata, smile bright as a competition floor. She's famous around town for her studio demos: how to drop someone with pressure points alone. With Meredith, she softens in a way she doesn't bother showing the rest of the world.

choices.text: You and Meredith close?
choices.response: She's the reason I don't punch walls. We fought like kids, we fight like adults now—but I'd step in front of a car for her.

clue.text: Emma describes fierce loyalty to Meredith—present tension is sisterly, not cold.

choices.text: How's the studio? And the cheer squad?
choices.response: The studio is my heart—but hearts don't pay rent. Coaching the cheer squad at the high school keeps the lights on while I figure the rest out. Meredith comes to games when shifts allow—she's my good-luck charm.

clue.text: Emma's martial arts studio isn't profitable—she coaches cheer at the high school to make ends meet.

choices.text: You and Alvin seem solid.
choices.response: He's… good to me. Patient. I'd marry him tomorrow if he asked. Meredith thinks I'm rushing—she says 'trust takes longer than love.' Big-sister wisdom.

clue.text: Emma wants to marry Alvin but he hasn't proposed—Meredith urges caution.

choices.text: Anything worrying you tonight besides Meredith turning thirty?
choices.response: Family stuff. Old wills. Nothing that should've stolen a birthday.

clue.text: Emma hints at 'old wills' and family money stress—touchy subject tonight.

post_initial.prompt: Emma's hands shake until she clenches them white. Grief and adrenaline look identical from across a room.

choices.text: You pulled Meredith aside before she collapsed. What was that about?
choices.response: Dad's will. Meredith got the house in the settlement—I rent half my life to banks. I asked her—begged—for a fairer split. She said she'd think. Then… then she couldn't breathe.

clue.text: Emma argued with Meredith about their father's will and unequal inheritance moments before death.

choices.text: Did Meredith seem ill earlier?
choices.response: Tired, maybe—happy tired. She wasn't gasping. She was Meredith until she wasn't.

clue.text: Emma saw no gradual illness—collapse appeared sudden.

choices.text: Did Meredith tell you anything about Tai? Maybe that he has been acting strange?
choices.response: Strange? She told me that he barely sleeps, barely talks. Meredith told me last week that he flinches every time his phone buzzes. She thought it was work stress but… maybe you need to speak with Alvin...

clue.text: Emma passes on Meredith's worries about Tai—withdrawn, jumpy at his phone—and suggests Nick talk to Alvin.

choices.text: Where were you during the toast?
choices.response: Glass in hand like everyone. I drank. Meredith drank. I didn't watch every milliliter—I'm not a hawk.

clue.text: Emma drank at the toast but didn't closely watch Meredith's glass.

choices.text: The will dispute, the money pressure — you had a reason to want things to go differently tonight.
choices.response: You think I'd hurt my own sister? I know a dozen ways to drop someone with my hands — pressure points, nerve strikes. If I wanted to hurt Meredith, I wouldn't need to be subtle about it.

clue.text: Emma insists she'd never hurt Meredith—and wouldn't need subtlety if she meant harm.

choices.text: Did you know Meredith was looking into Alvin?
choices.response: She told me. She said she hired someone to check his background — I thought she was being overprotective. But Meredith never does anything without a reason. She kept saying there was something about him she couldn't put her finger on. If Alvin found out she was digging…

clue.text: Emma knew Meredith was investigating Alvin — and wonders what would happen if Alvin found out someone was digging into his past.

choices.text: Alvin was planning to propose to you tonight. Did you know?
choices.response: He… what? No. No, I didn't—oh God. I spent the whole night angry about wills and money and he was—he had a ring? Tonight? While I was cornering Meredith about Dad's money, he was waiting to… and now my sister is dead... she is dead and things will never be the same...

clue.text: Emma had no idea Alvin planned to propose—she was consumed by the will dispute while he waited for the right moment.

emma_debt_skirt.prompt: Money hangs in the air whenever Emma says 'banks.'

choices.text: How bad is 'renting your life to banks'?
choices.response: Bad enough I don't sleep. Bad enough I hoped my sister might throw me a rope before lawyers did.

clue.text: Emma hints at severe debt and desperation for sisterly help—stops short of numbers.

secret.text: Alvin planned to propose to Emma tonight — had a ring in his jacket pocket.

initial.prompt: Alvin Mani's laugh is a beat too loud—performance, not joy. His eyelids droop without warning; he recovers with a self-deprecating joke about 'the world's rudest nap schedule.'

choices.text: How do you know the Marsh family?
choices.response: Emma's my girlfriend — that's the short version. I wasn't exactly invited, but Emma asked me to come last minute. Tai looked a bit surprised when I walked in.

clue.text: Alvin wasn't formally invited — Emma brought him last minute. Tai seemed surprised to see him.

choices.text: You look exhausted.
choices.response: Narcolepsy—not drunk, before anyone whispers that. I can fall asleep mid-sentence if my brain decides the world can wait.

clue.text: Alvin has narcolepsy—can sleep suddenly, relevant to timing around the toast.

choices.text: I've been asked to keep an eye on you tonight. Any idea why?
choices.response: Can't say I'm surprised. I'm not everybody's idea of a safe bet. But I'm here for Emma, and I'm trying to be someone worth keeping around. Tai? Ask him why he won't look me in the eye tonight.

clue.text: Alvin deflects about his own past but hints he's not 'a safe bet'—redirects suspicion toward Tai.

post_initial.prompt: Alvin rubs his temples. The bravado's gone; what's left is a man calculating legal exposure.

choices.text: Where were you during the toast?
choices.response: I was in the kitchen with Meredith — she wanted to talk about something — and then everything went dark. Narcolepsy hit me mid-sentence. When I came to, people were screaming. I never made the toast.

clue.text: Alvin missed the actual toast—narcolepsy micro-sleep—critical to cup confusion.

choices.text: If you missed the toast, which glass is yours?
choices.response: Natalie poured me water—she told me before the toast she had me covered. But when I woke up and took a sip, it was wine. Wine, Nick. I haven't touched alcohol in months and someone put wine in my glass.

clue.text: Alvin's glass was supposed to be water, but when he drank after waking up it was wine—the cups were switched.

choices.text: You seem angry at Natalie.
choices.response: She promised me. She looked me in the eye and said she had my back. Then I wake up to wine in my glass? Either she lied or someone swapped it. Either way, I almost—I could have spiraled tonight. Do you know what one sip does to months of work?

clue.text: Alvin is furious at Natalie — his water became wine. Either she lied or someone swapped his glass while he slept.

choices.text: You said Tai won't look you in the eye. What's really going on between you two?
choices.response: IP theft. He copied Delta's core inference stack. Monday I end him professionally unless lawyers negotiate a miracle.

clue.text: Alvin reiterates Monday as the reporting deadline—Tai's last window to act.

choices.text: Tell me everything about the stolen code—on the record.
choices.response: Weights, configs, enough to replicate our inference stack in a garage if you're unethical and patient. Tai has both.

clue.text: Alvin details severity of Tai's theft—enough to replicate Delta's inference stack.

choices.text: Could Tai have overheard your Monday plans?
choices.response: I told Emma I had documentation ready. Couples talk... Sisters talk...

clue.text: Alvin told Emma about Monday reporting—couples and sisters talk, so Tai might have learned through the family.

choices.text: What exactly is Tai sitting on?
choices.response: Proprietary model weights—core IP. He exfiltrated enough to build a shadow portfolio. I was going to report him Monday. Consequences, audits, maybe cuffs—depends how corporate wants blood.

clue.text: Alvin states Tai stole core Delta AI IP and he planned to report Tai Monday—strong motive for Tai to silence him.

suspects.name: Daniel "Film" Brown
suspects.role: Film critic, host of "Crime in a Small Town"

initial.prompt: Daniel Brown writes film reviews for the local paper — that's how he got the nickname 'Film.' Tonight the lapel mic clipped to his collar is for his podcast, not a review. He nods at you as if you're both in on the same punchline: small towns pretending they're boring.

choices.text: Recording tonight?
choices.response: The mic stays on out of habit—Meredith makes fun of me for it. She says I'd record my own funeral if the acoustics were good. Meredith's been my closest friend since we were sixteen. Tonight I'm just a guest.

clue.text: Daniel and Meredith are best friends since high school—the mic is just habit.

choices.text: What's the podcast working on?
choices.response: A cold case deep-dive—Adam Green, twenty years gone. Hanging, note, religious family, no autopsy. The ending's too tidy for good cinema—or good truth.

clue.text: Daniel is researching Adam Green's staged-looking suicide for his podcast.

choices.text: How does Meredith seem lately?
choices.response: Happy, I think. But careful—she's watching what she eats, watching what she drinks. Meredith doesn't usually hold back at her own party. Something's on her mind.

clue.text: Daniel notices Meredith is being unusually careful with food and drink tonight—something's off.

choices.text: Your podcast — you cover local cases?
choices.response: 'Crime in a Small Town.' Cold cases, mostly. People think nothing happens here — that's exactly the point. The quieter the town, the deeper the burial.

clue.text: Daniel's podcast covers local cold cases—he believes quiet towns hide the deepest secrets.

choices.text: You go to Elliot's shows?
choices.response: Every one. Skulls of Chaos is the only band in this town worth documenting. Elliot plays like he's angry at the guitar — it's beautiful. Meredith drags me when I forget.

clue.text: Daniel is a regular at Skulls of Chaos shows—close enough with Elliot and Meredith to be dragged along.

post_initial.prompt: Daniel's recorder is off, but his eyes keep scanning the room — old habits die hard, even when your best friend just did.

choices.text: Were you filming during the toast?
choices.response: Audio snag only—battery died. So all I've got is what I remember, and right now I don't trust any of it.

choices.text: Did you see anything odd between the toast and the collapse?

choices.text: What did your Adam Green research turn up?

He wanted to set up a program for at-risk youth. His childhood friends told me he dreamed of being a pilot. He also suffered from terrible migraines — bad enough he begged neighbors for compounding help. Nobody I interviewed expected him to take his own life.

choices.text: If Adam had all these plans, why would he kill himself?
choices.response: That's the question that won't let me sleep. People in town had meetings scheduled with him — that very day and the next — to advance the youth project. He didn't cancel a single one. No goodbye calls. No signs of depression. The whole thing felt scripted, not real.

clue.text: Daniel's sources say Adam had meetings scheduled the day he died and showed no signs of depression. The suicide story doesn't fit.

choices.text: Tell me about the suicide note.
choices.response: Short. Generic. 'I'm sorry, I can't do this anymore.' No names, no specifics, no personal detail. I've read enough scripts to know when dialogue doesn't fit the character. Adam's family took it at face value — their faith made suicide shameful enough to bury fast. They refused an autopsy on religious grounds. The town moved on.

clue.text: The suicide note was suspiciously generic — no personal details. The family refused an autopsy on religious grounds and buried the case fast.

choices.text: Was Meredith involved in your Adam Green research?
choices.response: She was pulling threads I couldn't reach. Meredith started asking around town about Adam — who his friends were, what Rose was like back then. She told me last week she thought the suicide story didn't add up. If Rose caught wind of that…

clue.text: Meredith was actively investigating Adam Green's death — asking around town and doubting the suicide verdict. Rose would have reason to worry.

choices.text: Does Adam's death resemble Meredith's?
choices.response: It's possible... but what is the connection? These deaths are 20 years apart!

clue.text: Daniel allows a possible parallel but questions what connects two deaths twenty years apart.

choices.text: Adam Green—your tenant. I need the truth, not the legend.

solution.reveal_narrative: You gather the survivors in the living room—the cake still half-cut, balloons nodding like guilty witnesses. Tai Marsh sits rigid on the arm of the sofa, but you watch his hands: they keep finding each other, twisting the wedding band he bought the year Meredith said yes. 'Tai never intended to poison Meredith - he loved her,' you begin. 'He poisoned Alvin Mani's cup—or thought he did. Alvin discovered Tai had stolen proprietary code from Delta AI. He planned to report Tai Monday morning. Alvin wasn't even on the guest list — Emma brought him last minute. When Tai saw him walk through the door, he made a decision. Silence him tonight, and the scandal vanishes with the weekend.' Alvin's jaw tightens; he doesn't deny the threat he posed. 'You obtained odorless, tasteless rodenticide from Rose White—legitimate, for a real pest problem. You dosed Alvin's cup during the party, then returned the bottle to Rose moments before the toast—so the murder weapon ended up in her bag, not your jacket. Natalie Apple poured only water into Alvin's glass and told you which one it was so you could hand it to him. During the delivery, you added drops to the cup she'd marked as his.' Tai starts to stand. You don't raise your voice—you let the logic pin him. 'Alvin's narcolepsy stole your window. He nodded off before the toast. Meredith was newly pregnant—only Dr. Rock knew from labs—and she was avoiding alcohol without explaining why to the room. She knew Alvin's cup held water. She swapped hers for his so she wouldn't have to drink wine. She toasted with the very dose meant for the man who could end your career.' Emma makes a sound like breaking glass. Rose White has gone gray. Natalie covers her mouth. 'The symptoms Lili recognized—air hunger, tetanic fists, the tongue—weren't performance. They were classic for what killed Adam Green twenty years ago. Adam was color-blind—something Rose never knew. Her color-coded system was invisible to him. He reached for the wrong bottle, and she's carried the weight of his death ever since, not understanding why he did it. History didn't repeat by accident tonight; it rhymed because you brought the same poison back into this house.' Tai's composure finally cracks and he collapses to the floor. 'I only wanted—he was going to destroy everything I built—' 'You destroyed Meredith,' you say softly. 'Your witness lived. Your wife and unborn child didn't.' Outside, a siren finally wails toward the house. For Meredith—who asked hard questions and trusted the wrong protector—it's far too late. For justice, it's barely on time.

wrong_coverup.bribed_officials: The town accepted faith and shame, not a bribery plot.
wrong_coverup.no_coverup: Rose absolutely altered how the death looked; denial of cover-up misses the staging.

cold_case_solution.reveal_narrative:
The second truth settles over the room like dust after an explosion—not as loud as Tai's guilt, but older, and buried deeper.

Adam Green wasn't a suicide. He was a tenant who trusted his landlady's routines: green bottle for the migraine compound Rose White measured for him when pharmacy work still lived in her hands. What Rose never knew—what no one told her—was that Adam was color-blind. He couldn't reliably tell crimson from forest green under lamplight. The day Rose was overwhelmed, she sent him to fetch his own dose. He reached for the red bottle—the rodenticide she kept separate—and drank poison thinking it was mercy.

Rose's face crumbles as the truth lands. For twenty years she believed Adam had chosen to die—that she'd merely failed to stop a tragedy already in motion. Learning now that her color-coding system, the one thing she trusted to keep people safe, was invisible to him—that breaks something deeper than guilt.

When she found him that day, panic outran conscience. A rope, a chair kicked away, a note in a hand that shook: the town saw a tragedy of youth and called it closed. The family's faith refused the cutting truth of an autopsy. Detective Nick Vince smelled staging even then—the angle of the ligature, the story that didn't sit—but proof stayed out of reach.

Tonight Meredith's body spoke a language Lili Rock remembered. That echo cracked Rose's silence. The bottles were never just props in a kitchen; they were bookends—one death ruled suicide, one framed as fate—both born from secrets kept too long in a small town that prefers neat endings to honest ones.

Adam's ledger closes without a noose around the truth: accidental poisoning by a woman who didn't know her safeguards were useless, then a cover-up that wore suicide's mask. Rose will answer for the staging. But the cruelest punishment may be the one she just received—learning that Adam never chose to die. He simply couldn't see the danger she'd painted red.
